text:
Predicates:
LocatedIn(x, y) ::: x is located in y.
MountainRange(x) ::: x is a mountain range.
Visited(x, y) ::: x visited y.
Mine(x) ::: x is a mine.
Donated(x) ::: x has been donated.
InRangeIn(x, y) ::: x is a mountain range in y.
HasMine(x) ::: x has a mine.
InRangeIn(x, y) ::: x is a mountain range in y.
HasMineIn(x, y) ::: x is a mountain range in y that has a mine.

Premises:
PicurisMountains(x) ∧ MountainRange(x) ∧ LocatedIn(x, newMexico) ∨ LocatedIn(x, texas) ::: The Picuris Mountains are in New Mexico or Texas.
Visited(juanDeOnate, x) ∧ LocatedIn(x, PicurisMountains) ::: Juan de Onate visited the Picuris Mountains.
Mine(y) ∧ LocatedIn(z, PicurisMountains) ∧ Donated(y) ∧ LocatedIn(z, PicurisMountains) ::: The Harding Pegmatite Mine, located in the Picuris Mountains, was donated.
¬∃x (MountainRange(x) ∧ LocatedIn(x, texas) ∧ HasMineIn(x, y) ∧ Donated(y)) ::: There are no mountain ranges in Texas with donated mines.

Conclusion:
LocatedIn(hardingPegmatiteMine, x) ∧ ¬LocatedIn(x, newMexico) ::: The Harding Pegmatite Mine is not located in a mountain range in New Mexico.
